pr_title: [release/8.0] Disable buffering of Blazor streaming responses
pr_body:
Backport of #53929 to release/8.0

/cc @halter73

# Disable buffering of Blazor streaming responses

## Description

This change disables response buffering and compression (edit: if compression would cause buffering) for streaming Blazor responses in the same way SignalR does for streaming SSE responses. It checks the state of the QuiescenceTask before writing the initial render to the response body to avoid unnecessarily disabling buffering for non-streaming responses.

Fixes #52323

## Customer Impact

Instead of seeing UI update immediately as new content becomes available which is the point of streaming rendering, the streaming component is only rendered after all the content arrives completely. This may be never depending on the design of the application.

This affects customers hosting Blazor apps on servers that buffer responses. This includes App Service and IIS Express in their default configurations. You can work around this by configuring the server to disable compression and buffering as described in the customer reported issue at #52323, but it's not discoverable. Nonetheless at least 5 customers have found this issue already.

## Regression?

- [ ] Yes
- [x] No

## Risk

- [ ] High
- [ ] Medium
- [x] Low

This change only affects streaming rendering which is new in .NET 8, and it uses a pattern already used by SignalR for SSE responses to disable buffering.

## Verification

- [x] Manual (required)
- [x] Automated

## Packaging changes reviewed?

- [ ] Yes
- [ ] No
- [x] N/A

issue_context.title: Blazor Stream Rendering not working on IIS Express
issue_context.body:
### Is there an existing issue for this?

- [X] I have searched the existing issues

### Describe the bug

When going to the weather forecasts page using IIS Express it waits for the 5 second delay and then shows the page.

The URL correctly changes but the page content doesn't until the forecast data is loaded.

![image](https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/assets/45168007/37796120-ddc1-4359-a16b-6250f89153f6)


### Expected Behavior

It should show the weather heading with the text "This component demonstrates showing data." and show "loading..." until the 5 second delay has finished then show the forecast data.

The below print screen is what we expect to happen. This was created by refreshing the forecasts page.

![image](https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/assets/45168007/729247b8-fb3e-446c-b436-61208cdea815)



### Steps To Reproduce

1. Scaffold the new Blazor web app template using settings shown here: ![image](https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/assets/45168007/c71f2496-d368-4928-9aac-cf41bcea0202)
2. Change the delay in weather.razor to 5000 to make the issue more obvious
3. Run the app using IIS Express in Visual Studio
4. Click on the Weather button

### Exceptions (if any)

_No response_

### .NET Version

8.0.100

comments:
Thanks for contacting us @brackers17 !
It seems that you are buffering the response in IIS, in order to benefit from streaming rendering you need to disable buffering at the IIS level.

Hi @brackers17. We have added the "Needs: Author Feedback" label to this issue, which indicates that we have an open question for you before we can take further action. This issue will be closed automatically in 7 days if we do not hear back from you by then - please feel free to re-open it if you come back to this issue after that time.

Setting this in your IIS config might help avoid the buffering (and at that point streaming rendering should work).
```
<configuration>
<system.webServer>
<handlers>
<add name="aspNetCore" path="*" verb="*" modules="AspNetCoreModuleV2" resourceType="Unspecified" responseBufferLimit="0" />
</system.webServer>
</configuration>
```

@surayya-MS I have tried updating the applicationHost.config file for IIS express with the above but I'm afraid it hasn't made a difference. 

Given that when you refresh the page it correctly comes back with "Loading..." does this not indicate that the IIS config was already correct?

I also experience the same problem but not just for "IIS Express" but also with "https" and "http" modes.
Just upgraded to VS17.8.1 and .net8
@brackers17 Are you also able to reproduce this without IIS (i.e. in "https", as above)?
@amcasey No, its working fine on https for me.
Yep, the same thing happens on my box.  Thanks for the detailed steps!
@ZeraGames Can you please file a separate issue.  If you're seeing problems that aren't confined to IIS, it may be unrelated (and we can always merge them again later).
The trace level logs for Kestrel and IIS are basically the same - just some server specific messages that appear in one but not the other.
@surayya-MS I think I managed to set the `responseBufferLimit` as you described (how can I confirm at runtime?) but it did not obviously change the behavior.
I have the same problem. I tried with IIS and also Kestrel. Both have the same issue.

> Setting this in your IIS config might help avoid the buffering (and at that point streaming rendering should work).
> 
> ```
> <configuration>
> <system.webServer>
> <handlers>
> <add name="aspNetCore" path="*" verb="*" modules="AspNetCoreModuleV2" resourceType="Unspecified" responseBufferLimit="0" />
> </system.webServer>
> </configuration>
> ```

I checked my web.config file and it's already the same as what you recommend.

Looks like the stream rendering is being compressed by default in IISExpress which makes the streaming part stop working.

You can fix this by modifying the `<repo root>/.vs/<app name>/config/applicationhost.config` file:
```
httpCompression directory="%TEMP%">
      <scheme name="gzip" dll="%IIS_BIN%\gzip.dll" />
      <dynamicTypes>
        <add mimeType="text/*" enabled="false" /> <!-- this is true by default -->
```

This would also probably occur if you install the dynamic compression module in IIS and enabled it for your app.
@ahmetsarikaya0696 If you're seeing problems in Kestrel too, that's probably a different issue.  Can you please file one and describe your setup and what you're seeing?

> @ahmetsarikaya0696 If you're seeing problems in Kestrel too, that's probably a different issue.  Can you please file one and describe your setup and what you're seeing?

I didn't change anything. Just created a project with sample pages. Only change I did is disabling nullable. If you ask for a specific folder or configuration I will be providing that.
I'm having similar issues with the stream rendering feature. When I run my application in `https` then it works as expected, but it does not work with `http` or `IIS Express` profiles

This seems to happen in the following circumstances:
* Streaming rendering is enabled.
* App is using enhanced navigation.
* Response is compressed by IIS (Express).

It works fine if not using enhanced nav (works on a regular server refresh).

With this in mind, I don't think there's anything that we can do on our side, other than documenting this. It's not possible to disable compression from JS, and it seems that either chrome or something else on the stack is buffering the entire response.

The recommendation here is to apply @BrennanConroy suggestion as you shouldn't be compressing dynamic HTML responses coming from Blazor (or any other SSR framework for that matter) by default as that opens you to BREACH attacks.

Pretty sure we did this hack to make it work with SignalR:

https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/blob/0ed0bcdbfd0e0ca1617179e495ef893e36cb332c/src/SignalR/common/Http.Connections/src/Internal/Transports/ServerSentEventsServerTransport.cs#L33-L41

I think this is the ~hack~ magic:
```C#
        context.Response.Headers.ContentEncoding = "identity";
```

@davidfowl that's good to know thanks!

That seems to do the trick!
We should attempt to patch this in .NET 8
@davidfowl I've already put it in the patch milestone 😄

Interesting. I'm seeing this issue only when deployed to App Service, not locally.
Mitigated the issue via adding _web.config_ with the following:
```
<configuration>
	<system.webServer>
		<urlCompression doStaticCompression="false" doDynamicCompression="false" />
	</system.webServer>
</configuration>
```

I was seeing this issue mostly when streaming enhanced form posts.

I turned off compression per the suggestions above for local dev, and intermediate responses streamed back worked intermittently.  Then I switched from IIS to Kestral for local development and the streaming now works well.

Although, it doesn't work when deploying to App Service (Windows)...which has IIS involved.  Turning off compression got the App Service to work intermittently.  But it'd be nice to have it work consistently, and I also don't like turning off compression.  

Ideally, there would be a way to turn off IIS compression/buffering just for enhanced form posts (or maybe Enhanced Nav in general).  Maybe there is already?

review_comments: Will this work if someone enables compression in Kestrel? Does it need to be configurable in that scenario?

The only way to enable compression in Kestrel is to use the middleware which respects the `DisableBuffering()` call above.

https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/blob/e1ebf00fbe63aa372051ef1c184895f169ca49f5/src/Middleware/ResponseCompression/src/ResponseCompressionBody.cs#L270-L283
